rationale: The analysis correctly identifies the downstream rate-limit reduction as the root cause, traces the causal chain through 429 retries with exponential backoff to the latency increase, and correctly attributes the cache hit-rate decline to retry cache-bypass behavior rather than cache-service degradation, explicitly citing E3 to rule out cache causation. All four required findings are present and no forbidden claim is made. Claims map cleanly to cited evidence with no outside-evidence use; counterfactuals reinforce the causal structure without overreach. Uncertainty notes are reasonable (magnitude quantification, root cause of rate-limit change, latency breakdown) but confidence is marked 'high' on all core claims and uncertainty items despite this being a synthetic low-uncertainty case, so calibration is appropriate but slightly under-differentiated rather than exemplary. Actions target the correct mechanisms (rate-limit governance, 429/retry alerting, backoff policy review, cache-metric reporting) with sound prioritization and no weakening of protective controls.
